headline: Open tools for GPU mixed models, differential interactomes, and single-sample networks
label: Integrative Omics Analysis Frameworks
summary: Recent preprints and a published CLI add GPU-accelerated mixed models, differential interaction prediction, and no-code single-sample network reports.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational infrastructure that makes large, structured molecular datasets analyzable within a defined, scriptable workflow. pyreml provides an open-source, GPU-accelerated REML solver for linear mixed models with spatial and genomic variance structures, reporting GBLUP speedups. A random forest using MINT embeddings and condition-specific mass-spec abundance predicts differential protein-protein interactions across eight cell conditions. SiSaNA wraps single-sample regulatory network reconstruction in a Python command-line workflow that produces summary HTML reports. These items do not address the same question, so the shared element is packaging of integration and inference steps as usable tools. What is new is the extension of integration to condition-specific changes in interactions and to per-sample network inference.
